target_customer: Small and mid-size teams, often remote, that want a lightweight shared knowledge base and notes tool
problem: Teams lost shared knowledge across chat and scattered docs and found tools like wikis heavy; Slite offered simple collaborative notes that integrate with Slack.
product_category: Team notes and knowledge base software

founders.name: Christophe Pasquier
founders.background_notes: YC page: French engineer and product person; a French report says Slite was his third company.

founders.name: Pierre Renaudin
founders.background_notes: Tech.eu (2020) says Pasquier and Renaudin founded Slite in 2016 at the eFounders studio; Slite's about page lists him as CTO.

competitors.name: Google Docs
competitors.traction_then: Ubiquitous; named by the CEO as the main competitor

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time collaborative editing and Slack integration are standard but non-trivial; built by a small team in six months.

defensibility.rationale: Documents create some lock-in, but note tools are crowded and easily copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Notion and Confluence became the usual comparisons by 2026 per Slite's own compare page; no incumbent bought Slite.

market_need_then: At launch Slite had 3,000 users from 250 companies by word of mouth after four months (VentureBeat, April 2018), showing demand for lightweight team docs.

branding.name_origin: Slite was originally short for satellite, per Slite's blog on its rebrand; it was reportedly first called NoteX per Hexa.

identity.logo: Rebranded logo based on the early satellite idea, done with StudioKoto

rebrands.why: To align with the vision of remote asynchronous communication; one Product Hunt user said the new icon looks like a loading state

branding.community_and_virality: Word-of-mouth growth reported in 2018; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself beyond the rebrand post; known mainly as a product.

outcome_analysis: Slite grew through word of mouth, raised a 4.4 million dollar seed in April 2018 and an 11 million dollar Series A in April 2020, and by 2026 reports over 1,700 customers and an AI-agent positioning. It stayed mid-sized in a crowded category dominated by Notion and Confluence, with no later round found.
notes: Hexa states the seed was in the HX17 program and that Slite began as NoteX (not opened). Founding year 2016 per Tech.eu versus 2017 per YC and Slite. No Series B found; CB Insights lists Series A as latest. Total raised 15 million per Tech.eu. YC page names only Pasquier; Renaudin added from Tech.eu.
